overview: Both contain a hydroxyl (–OH) group, but attached to very different carbon environments, giving them very different acidities and reactivities.
genZNote: Same –OH group, wildly different personality once it's attached to a benzene ring.

aspects.label: Structure
aspects.valueA: Hydroxyl (–OH) group attached to an sp³ carbon (alkyl group).
aspects.valueB: Hydroxyl (–OH) group attached directly to an aromatic (benzene) ring.

aspects.label: Relative Acidity
aspects.valueA: Weakly acidic to neutral; generally weaker acid than phenol.
aspects.valueB: Significantly more acidic than alcohols, due to resonance stabilization of the resulting phenoxide ion.

aspects.label: Reaction With NaOH
aspects.valueA: Does not react appreciably with aqueous NaOH.
aspects.valueB: Reacts with NaOH to form a soluble sodium phenoxide salt.
